{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABVyPIyg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzg_Ui3k", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 67, "title": "Add persistent model-asset cache management to the Chrome extension", "body": "## Problem

The Web translation processors (#65) already use best-effort Cache Storage for downloaded model assets, but the Chrome extension currently packages its ASR assets and has no explicit lifecycle or user-visible cache management for large optional models such as OPUS-MT (~239 MB) and TranslateGemma 4B (~3.1 GB).

We want the future extension to download optional models once on demand, reuse stored assets after Chrome restarts, and make download/cache status visible. Chrome extension storage is origin-isolated from the published Node Playground, so do not assume the Web page's existing model cache is shared with the extension. Cached assets are best-effort and may be evicted; never promise permanent retention.

## Expected outcome

Introduce the **smallest reusable model-asset cache capability for the Chrome extension**, without integrating translation inference or downloading a multi-GB model as part of this Issue.

Provide an extension-owned mechanism to:

- check whether a pinned model asset set is fully cached (`Not downloaded` / `Ready`);
- download/cache missing assets on explicit user request with `Downloading` progress and an `Error` state;
- reuse complete cached assets after closing/reopening the extension and restarting Chrome;
- handle incomplete/corrupt downloads, storage quotas, eviction and network failures safely, allowing retry;
- optionally delete a cached model's assets to reclaim space.

Keep inference local and keep this storage/caching concern separate from generic Pipeline routing. If an explicit cache/model-asset Node is useful, expose it as a concrete node/port dependency; do not introduce an implicit global RuntimeManager or a speculative plugin framework.

## Scope

- Reuse existing model URL/revision pinning and browser Cache Storage behavior where practical, adapting for the extension's own origin. Do not create a second competing cache for the same assets.
- Define a small manifest/asset-set description with immutable model ID/revision and required files. Cache readiness means **all** required assets are present and validated sufficiently to avoid treating partial downloads as ready.
- Provide a minimal extension UI/surface to initiate cache preparation and show status/progress for a small test asset set. It must be usable without launching translation inference or changing the current tab-transcription workflow.
- Treat large assets carefully: stream downloads or use bounded buffering where practical; avoid accidentally loading the full 3.1 GB model into JS memory solely for cache management.
- Consider `navigator.storage.persist()` as a best-effort durability improvement, but detect support and report the result accurately; do not assume it prevents eviction or user deletion.
- Keep permission/CSP changes minimal, justified and compatible with MV3. Do not add remote executable code.
- Document cache scope, download size/storage implications, Chrome restart behavior, eviction, offline limits and explicit model terms (especially Gemma) without silently mirroring/redistributing weights.
- Keep existing extension tab capture, bundled ASR, Node Playground and translation pages unchanged.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- Automated tests verify first-time download, progress, complete-cache detection, reuse after extension page/window recreation, interrupted/partial download retry, cache eviction, quota/network errors and optional deletion.
- A real isolated Chrome extension profile loads the packaged MV3 extension and exercises the cache UI and asset lifecycle with deterministic local fixture assets under its actual CSP.
- Reopening an extension page can detect previously stored complete assets without re-downloading them. A browser-context/profile restart test is included where practical; test reports distinguish profile persistence from guaranteed long-term retention.
- Cache keys are scoped to immutable model revisions and avoid collisions between different models/versions.
- Cached and missing files are distinguished; no partially cached asset set is reported as Ready.
- No raw user text/audio is uploaded by the cache feature; remote requests are limited to model assets.
- No actual 3.1 GB model download is required in default CI; tests use small fixtures. Any optional large-model smoke is clearly separate.
- Existing unit/browser/extension suites and extension packaging still pass.
- The implementation does not add translation inference to the extension or change the existing ASR workflow.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Real-user device persistence and multi-GB download performance are useful optional follow-up validation, not mandatory human acceptance gates.

## Context

- #7 — local-first composable pipeline vision.
- #61 — extension uses shared Node/Port pipeline.
- #65 — OPUS-MT and TranslateGemma 4B translation nodes; their Web implementation already uses Cache Storage best-effort.
- `docs/translation-nodes.md` documents model sizes, pinned revisions, asset loading and license constraints.

This is intentionally the **extension cache foundation first**.
